column1: # AN EXAMPLE BASKET RULER, not a default: no set grades a basket unless a run names a ruler
# (`-basketruler`). SMH's eight largest holdings as of 2026-10-02 -- NVDA TSM AMD AVGO MU INTC AMAT
# KLAC -- against QQQ, adjusted closes from Yahoo's public chart API. To re-measure: write the nine
# symbols' adjusted closes as one wide CSV (`date,QQQ,NVDA,...`) and run `record_bands -basket
# -closes WIDE.csv -closesdate D -from 2012-01-04 -to 2026-08-31`; a later fetch reads slightly
# differently, every distribution since recomputing the adjusted series. The `dials` group is
# THE BASKET RULER for `-basketruler`: 8 names against QQQ, measured by
# `record_bands -basket` from a wide closes file (adjusted closes, dividends reinvested, taken
# Every row is `basket_read`'s, the reading the model takes of each path under this file's
# coverage: a name counts from its first close on, and a model path reads name k over its
# coverage span (start..end of the window's sessions) scaled to the path. A name under
# minSessions sessions stays in the aggregate and the tail coincidence and out of the per-name
# and pair ranges. `-solvebasket` writes the `dials` group.
